sb_prompt: HAVE YOU DONE ANY PAINTING PROJECTS RECENTLYY
turns: Yeah, actually I did start a couple of landscapes last week, just messing around with oils in my spare room. What about you?
Oh wow, that's nice! I actually tried acrylics once about ten years ago, but honestly I just didn't feel like it clicked for me, so I kind of quit cold turkey.
Right, I get what you mean, mostly the fact that you can't seem to get the colors to actually sit right on the canvas is the thing that makes people quit cold turkey.
Yeah, it's just frustrating because you can't really fix it once it's dry, whereas with watercolors at least you can lift paint back up.
Yeah, I know the feeling, though I'm still stubbornly trying to get those greens to look like grass instead of just... swamp water.
Yeah, it's that weird sticky stage where everything just looks muddy before it even dries that really kills it for me.
Right, so maybe you should stick with watercolors, or at least try that first?
Yeah, watercolors are a bit more forgiving, but honestly, I never really got past the sketching part anyway.
Look, I think it's just about patience, you know? You gotta let the layers breathe or it gets all gloopy like that.
Yeah, I guess that's the thing with me, I never really stuck with it long enough to figure out how to let it dry.
Yeah, it's that specific kind of patience, you know? Like, you have to trust the chemistry, but with oils, it's almost like the paint is holding a grudge against you for even touching it.
That's a good point about the chemistry, but I don't think it's about the paint, it's just that I'm too busy grading papers to sit still for days.
Exactly, I mean I only have about an hour between shifts at the bank so I can't even sit still for hours, and honestly that's probably why my greens are looking a bit muddy.
Yeah, that's probably it too, honestly I made up my mind years ago to just be too busy for art.
Look, nobody makes time for hobbies, that's the tragedy of it, but I'm still here trying to mix that yellow and blue and hope it doesn't turn green again.

Yeah, I get that, but I'm just stuck in this weird loop where I feel like painting would be this grand, life-changing thing if I actually had the time, so I guess I just keep sitting there waiting for the right moment that never comes.
Yeah, that grand life-changing thing always ends up being just sitting on the couch mixing colors while your coffee gets cold.
I guess I'm just used to fixing someone else's mistakes, so painting my own world feels like too risky a bet.

Yeah, that makes sense, fixing other people's stuff is a whole different mindset, but it feels a little too safe, don't you think? I mean, I'd rather mess up my own greens and learn from it than never try at all.
Yeah, there's a whole different kind of pressure when you're holding someone else's trust instead of just your own vision.
Yeah, but I think there's something to be said for just owning your own mess, even if it is a big muddy green swamp.
Yeah, maybe I should just go for the messy swamp thing myself sometime instead of always trying to fix everyone else's messes.
Yeah, I think once you stop trying to fix the mess and just let it breathe, you might finally find some grass.

That's actually a pretty good way to look at it. I think I might just pick up a brush tomorrow and make the swamp look intentional. Maybe I'll even bring my art supplies into the staff lounge so I can practice while grading. What do you think?
That's a bold move if you ask me, but hey, a muddy swamp is better than a blank page, right?
Yeah, I'll definitely do that, and if the staff lounge gets too crowded I can probably just sketch right there at my desk between periods.
That's the plan, and hey, at least then I won't have to worry about getting paint on my uniform before shift ends.
Yeah, if I start painting on the desk, we'll definitely need some kind of code to signal when I'm ready to hand back the papers.
That sounds like a solid code, maybe just three taps?
That works, just tap twice to keep it simple.
Yeah, double taps it is, but hey, don't let the supply room run out of solvents while you're waiting.
Oh, definitely no running out on you, I've got a stash of cheap ones in my car just in case I get stuck during lunch.
That's a clever backup plan, just make sure you don't forget to wash your hands before you go back to grading those essays.
Yeah, good idea, just don't forget to wipe the desk down before I start handing out the next batch of quizzes.
Yeah, wipe it down real good before you sit back down or you're going to be working on a sticky mess.
Yeah, just wipe it down real quick so I don't get paint all over the student papers.
Yeah, just wipe it off real quick before you start handing out the next batch of quizzes.
That sounds good, I'll get the wipe ready before the bell rings.
Sounds like a plan, just don't let the paint bleed into the quiz bubbles if you can help it.
Yeah, don't want to ruin the answer key bubbles, just a little dab won't hurt.
